name: Itutang-Inapang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University.
sources.note: p.13 (p.22): identical sentence — stress marking omitted because 'the stress patterning has not been well established yet'. No language-specific suprasegmental statement for Itutang/Midsivindi.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page inap1241 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Bibliography has zero grammar/grammar-sketch/phonology items; only Z'graggen overviews/wordlists, Ethnologue, ISO change requests.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-253: retire [itu] Itutang, merge into [mzu] Inapang (submitted by Daniel Moore, New Tribes Mission, Goroka; adopted 2008-01-14).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; identity only ('Itutang is the name of one village within the Inapang language'); submitter cites three years of first-hand work with the group — evidence that unpublished NTM language materials may exist.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Nothing: village/census checklist and maps only (Itutang = M5, Midsivindi = M6).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: Australian National University. viii+187 pp.
sources.note: p.6 (methods): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Tamolan family section (pp.80-82) lists Itutang (no.59) and Midsivindi (no.60) with villages and lexicostatistics; 'Typological Characteristics of Tamolan' (p.82) gives segmental notes only (alveopalatal stop in Midsivindi, words tend to end in a vowel, Romkun possibly tonal) — nothing on stress for Itutang/Midsivindi.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG language resources for Inapang [mzu] (pnglanguages.sil.org/resources/search/code/mzu) — check for any survey report, Organised Phonology Data or dialect survey of the Tamolan/Goam area.
sources.note: Could not be reached by automated download (an automated-access block). If an SIL sociolinguistic survey or OPD exists for Inapang or the Itutang-Midsivindi area it would likely include a stress note.

sources.note: Only substantial primary data on Itutang and Midsivindi (Inapang); phonetic transcriptions might carry stress marks despite the 1971 disclaimer, allowing a pattern to be read off.

sources.citation: New Tribes Mission / Ethnos360 (Daniel Moore et al.), c. 2004-2010. Unpublished Inapang phonology statement / orthography paper / grammar notes produced for the NTM Inapang program (existence inferred from ISO 639-3 CR 2007-253: 'Three years of working with the language group').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only party known to have done sustained first-hand linguistic work on Inapang; NTM programs routinely write a phonemic statement that fixes stress for orthography decisions. Would be the sole primary statement on Inapang stress if it exists.
